proof.claim:
A node with no prior state must be able to join, install its services, and
converge — the Day-1 path, exercised as a FIRST join rather than a re-join.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The suite already had node-join-convergence, but it asserts
target_node_registered_before: it stops and restarts a node that is already a
cluster member, so it exercises re-join and never the path a genuinely new
machine takes. The distinction is not academic — the bootstrap unit
short-circuits on an "already bootstrapped" marker in the node's state volume:

    [bootstrap] already bootstrapped (day0 ...) — nothing to do

so a node whose state survives never runs the join at all.

On 2026-08-17 that gap cost hours. A gateway carried forward from an older
base bundle still ran a join step installing libnss-resolve, a package the
release deliberately no longer ships, and every joining node died:

    FAIL: package libnss-resolve not found in /var/lib/globular/packages
    [bootstrap] FATAL: join failed

The founding node bootstrapped normally, so the cluster reported HEALTHY at
one node while four could never join. Nothing in 74 scenarios would have
caught it; it was found by reading journals. That is the shape this scenario
closes — a join failure that presents as "still converging".

WHAT IT PINS. Wipe a node's state completely, restart it, and require that it
comes back as a full member: registered in etcd, services installed, running,
and the cluster healthy with every node accounted for. It asserts the OUTCOME
of the join rather than any particular step, so it stays valid as the join
procedure changes — which it does, and which is how it broke.

This scenario is destructive by design and slow: a real first join installs
the full service set.

authority.note: Simulation output is evidence/candidate knowledge only. Governed promotion is required before production may rely on it.
